title: Analyze the record in SBD-SPLUNK01
subtitle: Search a working copy, own the alerts, prove the chain
description: The last of three logging courses: build SBD-SPLUNK01 as a domain-joined Linux server patched only from SBD-REPO01, install Splunk Enterprise from hashed media, forward the collector's two streams over TLS, build the searches that answer this network's first questions, turn them and the pipeline's own failures into alerts someone owns, and trace one event from its source through the collector and the repository to the analyst's screen.
outcomes: Plan analysis — indexes, 90-day retention, roles, and console paths — and build SBD-SPLUNK01 on domain time, patched only from SBD-REPO01.
Install Splunk Enterprise and forward the collector's two streams over TLS, with counts and times that match the collector.
Build the working searches and turn them, and the pipeline's own failures, into tested alerts with named responders.
Trace one event from its source through the collector and the repository to the analyst's screen.

stages.title: Plan analysis and build SBD-SPLUNK01
stages.detail: Analysis works on a copy, not on the record: SBD-AUDIT01 keeps the evidence, and SBD-SPLUNK01 keeps 90 days of searchable events for the people who question them. Decide the indexes, retention, roles, and console paths first, then build the domain-joined Linux host that runs it — patched only from SBD-REPO01 and on domain time from its first boot.

stages.title: Install Splunk and bring in the streams
stages.detail: Install Splunk Enterprise on SBD-SPLUNK01 with the indexes, roles, and TLS receiving port lesson 1 designed, then put a universal forwarder on SBD-SYSLOG01 that reads the collector's two streams and sends them over rule F10. Finish by proving the copy is faithful: Splunk's counts and times must match the collector's.

stages.title: Build the working searches
stages.detail: Analysis earns its place with three working searches: failed privileged sign-ins, the boundary's denies, and the health of time — questions this network can already answer about itself. Build them as an analyst, prove each against an event you caused, and save them for the alerts in lesson 4.

stages.title: Own the alerts
stages.detail: An alert nobody owns is a log entry with extra steps. Turn the working searches and the pipeline's own failure conditions into scheduled alerts, each with a threshold, a named responder, and a written first response; test each one by causing it, tune the noise, and set the review cadence AU-6 asks for.

stages.title: Prove the chain and hand off
stages.detail: One deliberate event, followed all the way: a failed privileged sign-in should appear on the source, the collector, the analyst's screen, and the repository's next-morning archive. That trace closes all three logging courses; SBD-SPLUNK01's first baseline and the handoff to the fleet close this one.

outcomeSummary: A working copy that answers real questions, alerts someone owns, and one event traced through all three logging systems.
